A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 33-page versions of Separation Power of Equivariant Neural Networks, including Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, figures, and proofs support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports theoretical characterizations, proofs, and analytical examples, including applications to IGNs and circular CNNs. Neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: V3 retains the theoretical study and analytical applications. No original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis results appear in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: The neural-space construction, twin-network trick, recursive characterization, and network families remain unchanged. The appendix correction concerns mathematical map definitions, not a revised network or algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. IGNs and circular CNNs remain analytical applications with the same scope.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. The theoretical comparisons with k-WL and between network families are retained.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol, data splits, training budgets, or empirical metrics. No such settings are introduced.

E4.justification: The analytical examinations of activation, depth, representation choice, and filter support are unchanged. Neither version contains experimental ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. The stated separability findings for activations, depth, hidden width, IGNs, and circular CNNs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5, page 18, generalizes the induced precomposition and postcomposition maps from R^G to an arbitrary representation V. Definition 11 then specifies one composition order instead of the earlier two-order equality. This resolves a domain/codomain mismatch in the definitions; the main theorems and subsequent proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusions retain the same claims about exact separation characterization, non-polynomial activations, depth stabilization, feature-width independence, and representation hierarchies.

C2.justification: The interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations concerning permutation representations, bias terms, and polynomial activations.

D1.justification: Neither version provides experimental implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data release instructions. Bibliography URL changes concern cited literature rather than reproducibility resources for this work.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and positioning against previous expressivity results are unchanged. The bibliography revises metadata for matched references without introducing a new research comparison.

P1.justification: V3 adds Section 9 acknowledgements, changes the publication-status header, and makes isolated wording corrections in Section 4.1 and the Theorem 3 proof outline. Bibliographic entries are shortened and updated; the scientific narrative and organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements and shortened bibliography reflow pages 11–13, alongside header and minor typesetting changes. Figure 1 and the appendix diagrams retain their content and placement; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: The Appendix A.5 revision repairs the incompatible map domains underlying Definition 11, providing a limited gain in mathematical precision. Bibliographic editing introduces a countervailing weakness: Geerts and Reutter remains cited as 2022 but is listed as 2020 in v3. The localized mathematical repair supports a small overall improvement, with the main claims and proofs unchanged.
